introduction: Ten symbols, events, and locations are considered supremely auspicious in Jainism. These Pancha Teerthankara or sacred symbols are used in worship, temple architecture, meditation, and daily Puja.

symbols.name: Swastika
symbols.meaning: May all beings be happy and well. The four arms represent the 4 states of existence: heavenly, human, animal, and hellish. The four points also represent the Four Jewels of Jainism.
symbols.usage: Drawn in rice or sand before every Puja; drawn on new account books; drawn on temples and mandalas.

symbols.name: Siddhashila
symbols.meaning: The crescent moon and dot at the top of the Jain Symbol representing the eternal abode of liberated Siddhas at the apex of the universe.
symbols.usage: Represents the goal of all spiritual practice; drawn at the top of altars; used in meditation on liberation.

symbols.name: Three Dots (Ratnatraya)
symbols.meaning: The three dots below the Swastika representing Right Faith, Right Knowledge, and Right Conduct — the path to liberation.
symbols.usage: Drawn in Puja; meditated upon as the ladder of spiritual ascent.

symbols.name: Ahimsa Hand / Palm
symbols.meaning: The raised palm with the wheel (Ahimsa Chakra) inscribed with 'Ahimsa' — the supreme vow of non-violence. It means 'Stop! Think before you act, lest you harm any living being.'
symbols.usage: Used in all Jain ceremonies, drawn on entryways, worn as pendants, used in meditation.

symbols.name: Kalasha
symbols.meaning: The sacred water pot symbolizing prosperity, purity, and the 14 dreams of Tirthankara's mother. Used in all auspicious ceremonies.
symbols.usage: Filled with holy water and coconut; placed at temple entrances; used during Puja and Utsavas.

symbols.name: Om
symbols.meaning: The primordial sound of the universe. In Jainism, Om is the condensed form of the five lines of the Navkar Mantra: A-A-A-U-M. It represents the essence of the supreme beings.
symbols.usage: Chanted as meditation; written on sacred texts; painted on temple walls; the sound with which Jainism begins and ends.

symbols.name: Ashta Mangalas
symbols.meaning: The eight auspicious symbols placed around the footprint of the Jina in temple rituals. Each represents a supreme quality of the liberated soul.
symbols.usage: Arranged in ritual Puja; used in wedding and religious ceremonies; drawn on mandalas.

symbols.name: Shrimala (Srivatsa)
symbols.meaning: The auspicious mark on the chest of all Tirthankaras, resembling a upward-pointing triangle or a small diamond. It is the symbol of supreme spiritual royalty and marks the Tirthankara's pure soul.
symbols.usage: Drawn on the chest of Tirthankara idols; used in religious art; represents the spotless soul.

symbols.name: Chaitya Vriksha
symbols.meaning: The sacred tree under which Tirthankaras attain Kevala Jnana and deliver sermons. It symbolizes the tree of Dharma (spiritual law) under which shelter is sought.
symbols.usage: Found in every Jain temple; used in meditation; represents the shelter of Dharma.

symbols.name: Dharma Chakra
symbols.meaning: The wheel of dharma representing the teachings of the Jina. It has 24 spokes (for the 24 Tirthankaras) and represents the cosmic rhythm of Samsara and liberation.
symbols.usage: Spun in festivals; painted on temple walls; meditated upon as the wheel of cosmic law.
